title: fswatch: watch late-created herd dir, clear header error on recovery
description:
Reviewer nit 4 from epic zz0, human-approved fix. internal/herd/dashboard/fswatch.go has two degrade-only gaps: (a) if .tick/logs/herd does not exist when the dashboard starts, addWatches fails for it and the directory is NEVER watched afterwards - a tk herd spawn that creates it after dashboard start gets no fast-path manifest reloads (only the 30s ticker); (b) after any fsw.Errors emission the dashboard header shows the fswatch error forever - nothing re-emits an Up/healthy signal even though the watcher keeps delivering events and reloads keep flowing.

Fix: (a) when the herd logs dir is missing at start, watch its nearest existing ancestor (.tick/logs or .tick) for the create event and add the real watch (and epic-subdir watches) when it appears - or re-attempt on the debounced reload path; pick the approach that fits the existing structure (read fswatch.go + its tests + doc.go first) and say why. (b) after a successful event delivery or reload following an error, emit the healthy state so the header clears - mirror however the events-down/reconnecting indicator clears in the watch.go stream path (read it; be consistent with that pattern).

Tests (extend the existing real-fsnotify test style): start without the herd dir, create it + a manifest -> fast-path reload fires (not just ticker); error then recovery -> header state transitions error -> healthy. Boundaries: internal/herd/dashboard only. Full-suite gate on real exits; gofmt/vet clean. Do NOT commit your RESULT file.
